title: Defoliation Interval and Balanced Fertilisation of High-Andean Ryegrass–White Clover Pastures: Forage Yield, Nutrient Balance and Dairy Cow Responses
content: In the northern Peruvian highlands, milk production depends on ryegrass–white clover pastures that are rarely fertilised and used at long regrowth intervals. Two independent studies were conducted in 2024 at 3482 m a.s.l. Experiment 1 combined four balanced fertilisation levels (0–156 kg N ha−1 with macro- and micronutrients) and four cutting intervals (30–75 d) in a split-plot design over two cycles. In the rainy cycle, fertilisation raised yield per cut from 2216 (F0) to 4120 kg DM ha−1 (F2), with no gain at the highest rate. Daily productivity peaked at 60 d, but quadratic optima were imprecise. With 30- and 45-d cutting, third-cut yield fell to 53–57% of the first. Each additional regrowth day lowered crude protein by 0.11 and in vitro digestibility by 0.24 percentage points. With 60-d cutting, N and K2O removal exceeded inputs in every treatment. Experiment 2 compared two consecutive 12-day periods with the same 11 cows: traditional pasture and resown, fertilised pasture grazed at 42 d. In the second period, intake was 3.27 kg DM cow−1 d−1 higher, and milk yield 2.92 kg cow−1 d−1 higher (+30%), with unchanged milk composition. Because we did not replicate the order of the periods, we cannot attribute these differences solely to pasture management.
